MC	<p>edc9_769d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kt, ++, kt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>395b_ec3c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5f4aae;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kw, ++, kw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cfeb_9195</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e48;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #166e48;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e48;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5f4aae;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fk, ++, fk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3318_dcae</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #07629e;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #07629e;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d413_99b9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hy, ++, hy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a4db_3df6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8e30_3eed</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8776_6458</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ht, ++, ht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e59a8;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3e59a8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #07629e;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #07629e;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3c50_b8a9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e59a8;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3e59a8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e48;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #166e48;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e48;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c3156;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9c3156;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7950_4ae5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #944406;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #944406;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #944406;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hr, ++, hr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>438e_09b7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dr, ++, dr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>36bc_aa7c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9882_8a60</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1b47_103c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #944406;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #944406;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #944406;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #07629e;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #07629e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>2ccf_8f9d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ex, ++, ex"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">9,000</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> MC	<p>72ab_0cbe</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>50b4_0385</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e48;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #166e48;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e48;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c3156;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c3156;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3826_a8c3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5f4aae;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ah, ++, ah"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>315f_571e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f4aae;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5f4aae;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>78c0_3258</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e59a8;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3e59a8;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c640b;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5c640b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c640b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e59a8;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3e59a8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e59a8;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pt, ++, pt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">8,400</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>d76c_7d48</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c640b;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5c640b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c640b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f915_9d01</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ky, ++, ky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">4,000</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>13eb_e455</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ep, ++, ep"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">8,400</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>ec1b_2134</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7e3aa1;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7e3aa1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3c6c27;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>dd88_7c49</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cy, ++, cy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b06b_793e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #944406;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #944406;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #944406;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #166e48;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #166e48;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e48;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fk, ++, fk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>05f3_982a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ak, ++, ak"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0c11_5a9d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kt, ++, kt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0ded_f0c8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bn, ++, bn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c27;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #07629e;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #07629e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c640b;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5c640b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>351a_3285</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d372d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d372d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #166e48;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #166e48;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e48;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ek, ++, ek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
